schema_notes: Bean-editable. route.py re-reads on every call. v6 (2026-10-17): the 5.5 generation (Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5) with an effort level on every answer; Sonnet is the workhorse for dispatched work, including multi-file code and debugging; Opus 5.5 is a dispatch tier for hard self-contained work; Haiku 5.5 is for bounded find-and-list and mechanical work only; a cloud tier for long code-only jobs; a fan-out budget and brief lines every dispatch carries. Budget gating and the dispatch log were removed: the log recorded no token counts, so nothing could be calibrated or budgeted from it.

fanout.notes: A session normally runs no more than 3 subagents at once and about 12 in total; .claude/settings.json sets CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS=4 as the hard ceiling. Past the soft cap, do the next piece of work inline unless it is a genuinely independent, sizeable track. Each subagent re-establishes context, re-explores and reports back, and the main session then reads its report, so fan-out multiplies cost and wall-clock time; one subagent beats several on a modest task.

brief_must_include: Time matters here: do not spend time that can be avoided, and the earlier a correct result is obtained, the better.
Match your checking to the risk: a low-risk change needs one real check that exercises it, not layers of review.
Return only what the caller needs: findings or results with file paths, no narrative of what you did.

haiku.reliability_notes: Bounded find-and-list work: locating files and call sites, listing usages, extraction, classification, summarising, and mechanical edits with an exact spec. Weak at agentic coding (about 39% on Anthropic's coding-agent benchmark against Sonnet 5.5's 71%) and at judgement. Keep it at medium effort: higher effort made it slower and wordier with no accuracy gain. Its price is lowest with prompts under about 100K tokens.

sonnet.reliability_notes: The default for dispatched work. Strongest on multistep agentic coding in a real repository: multi-file code changes, debugging, code review, MCP and Playwright work, research and large-input synthesis. Use medium effort for coding and tool work, low for simple jobs, high for hard debugging. At low effort it can report code done without running a check, so the brief lines require a real check.

opus.reliability_notes: Hard, self-contained work that needs deep reasoning but not this conversation's context: root-causing a stubborn bug, an architecture or security review, reviewing Sonnet's work. About twice Sonnet's price. It checks its own work unprompted, so do not ask it to add verification layers.

cloud.command: Bash from a local session: claude --cloud "<self-contained prompt>" (push the branch first; collect the result with claude --teleport <session-id> or by merging its branch)
cloud.reliability_notes: A Claude Code on the web session that runs on Bean's separate cloud credits, not the Max allowance. It starts from GitHub only: no SSH key, no sgs-framework.db, no .claude/secrets, no node_modules and nothing from ~/.claude, and it cannot message the local session back. Fit: long (20 minutes or more), code-only work such as a code review, writing a fix the local session will test, doc reconciliation, or a plan executed against the repo. Never: deploys, reseeds, live-site probes or anything needing credentials.

inline.command: (do not dispatch, handle in main conversation)
inline.reliability_notes: The current conversation. Use when the work needs this conversation's context, for strategic decisions, for quick targeted changes, and for sensitive content.

then.justification: Strategic work stays inline (2026-04-18 correction). Only qc_review and persona_panel may be delegated for this class of work; both have their own rules and both report back inline.
No dispatch criterion met (subagent-prompt Stage 1). Inline wins for connected reasoning and quick changes.
Content signal: credentials or secrets. Keeping them in the main thread minimises copies across subagent transcripts.
Content signal: personal data. Stays in the main thread to minimise copies across subagent transcripts.
Content signal: suspected prompt injection. A cold Sonnet subagent keeps the suspect content out of the main thread.
MCP tools (Playwright, GitHub and others) run through the local Agent tool; Sonnet is the MCP dispatch tier. A cloud session has none of the local MCP servers.
Long, code-only work that needs nothing outside GitHub runs as a cloud session on Bean's separate cloud credits, and the local session stays free. Results come back as a branch.
Web search runs through the /search skill in the main thread; subagents cannot invoke search.py reliably.
Destructive work (DB migration, mass rewrite) needs worktree isolation, which the local Agent tool provides.

Persona panel (brainstorming council, research council, critique pairs): up to 3 cold Sonnet subagents, each primed with a distinct persona, so independence comes from cold context and divergent priming. Each persona reports back briefly; the main session synthesises; findings surface to Bean before anything is applied.

Bounded find-and-list or mechanical work with an exact spec: Haiku 5.5 at medium effort gets it right at a fraction of the cost and faster. Escalate to Sonnet when the job turns out to need judgement.
Batch synthesis: Sonnet's 1M window takes the large input. Keep the synthesis inline when it is itself a strategic decision.

inline.note: The main session did the work: a cold Sonnet reviewer (different tier, fresh context).

sonnet.note: Sonnet did the work: a cold Opus reviewer, which keeps the main session free.

opus.note: Opus did the work: a cold Sonnet reviewer.

haiku.note: Haiku did the work: Sonnet reviews.

then.justification: QC is cross-tier: the reviewer is a different Claude tier from the author, dispatched cold so it shares no context with the authoring thread. route.py refuses to answer without original_model.
Code review needs code understanding and multi-file reasoning: Sonnet's strength.

Hard, self-contained work (multi-hop reasoning, stubborn root cause, architecture review): Opus 5.5 at high effort. If the work needs this conversation's context, the dispatch is not justified and it stays inline.
Debugging: Sonnet at high effort. Escalate to Opus only after Sonnet has failed to find the root cause.
Input above about 100K tokens moves Haiku 5.5 onto its higher rate card and past its sweet spot for bounded work; Sonnet takes it.

Default: Sonnet 5.5 at medium effort handles code generation, multi-file changes and unclassified dispatch work reliably. Bounded lookups route to Haiku and hard self-contained work to Opus through higher-priority rules.
